      </feMerge>
    </filter>
  </defs>
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0F1729"/>
  <!-- Title bar -->
  <rect x="40" y="40" width="6" height="36" fill="url(#titleGrad)" rx="3"/>
  <text x="60" y="68" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold" fill="#E2E8F0">Agent Skills Remain Static After Deployment</text>
  <!-- Left column: Static paradigm -->
  <rect x="40" y="110" width="580" height="520" rx="12" fill="#1A2744" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="40" y="110" width="580" height="44" rx="12" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
  <rect x="40" y="142" width="580" height="12" rx="0" fill="#1A2744"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-x" x="60" y="118" width="28" height="28" fill="#EF4444"/>
  <text x="96" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#EF4444">Static Skill Paradigm (Current)</text>
  <!-- Static paradigm bullet points -->
  <text x="68" y="188" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Skills manually installed from centralized hub</text>
  <text x="68" y="228" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Solutions discovered during interaction</text>
  <text x="68" y="248" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">never persist beyond individual sessions</text>
  <text x="68" y="292" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Same patterns of failure and recovery</text>
  <text x="68" y="312" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">repeatedly observed across users</text>
  <text x="68" y="356" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Each user forced to rediscover solutions</text>
  <text x="68" y="376" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">independently</text>
  <!-- Existing approaches box -->
  <rect x="60" y="416" width="540" height="200" rx="8" fill="#0F1729" fill-opacity="0.6"/>
  <text x="80" y="446" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#94A3B8">EXISTING APPROACHES FALL SHORT</text>
  <rect x="80" y="460" width="100" height="2" fill="#334155"/>
  <text x="80" y="490" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.9">Memory-based:</text>
  <text x="200" y="490" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#94A3B8">Store trajectories but tied to</text>
  <text x="200" y="510" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#94A3B8">specific instances, hard to generalize</text>
  <text x="80" y="550" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#EF4444" fill-opacity="0.9">Skill-based:</text>
  <text x="200" y="550" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#94A3B8">Compress into structured instructions</text>
  <text x="200" y="570" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" fill="#94A3B8">but treat library as static resource</text>
  <!-- Right column: Evolving paradigm -->
  <rect x="660" y="110" width="580" height="520" rx="12" fill="#1A2744" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="660" y="110" width="580" height="44" rx="12" fill="#22C55E" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
  <rect x="660" y="142" width="580" height="12" rx="0" fill="#1A2744"/>
  <use data-icon="circle-checkmark" x="680" y="118" width="28" height="28" fill="#22C55E"/>
  <text x="716" y="140" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="18" font-weight="bold" fill="#22C55E">Evolving Skill Paradigm (SkillClaw)</text>
  <!-- Evolving paradigm points -->
  <text x="688" y="188" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Skills continuously evolve from</text>
  <text x="688" y="208" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">runtime interaction evidence</text>
  <text x="688" y="252" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Cross-user trajectories aggregated</text>
  <text x="688" y="272" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">for complementary behavioral signals</text>
  <text x="688" y="316" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Agentic evolver performs open-ended</text>
  <text x="688" y="336" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">reasoning over evidence</text>
  <text x="688" y="380" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#E2E8F0">Updated skills verified and synced</text>
  <text x="688" y="400" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">back to all agents automatically</text>
  <!-- Arrow between columns -->
  <polygon points="635,370 650,360 650,380" fill="#3B82F6" fill-opacity="0.8"/>
  <rect x="636" y="366" width="18" height="8" fill="#3B82F6" fill-opacity="0.3" rx="2"/>
  <!-- Key insight box -->
  <rect x="688" y="440" width="530" height="80" rx="8" fill="#3B82F6" fill-opacity="0.1"/>
  <rect x="688" y="440" width="4" height="80" fill="#3B82F6" rx="2"/>
  <text x="712" y="468" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#3B82F6">Key Insight</text>
  <text x="712" y="494" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#E2E8F0">Knowledge accumulates at the system level,</text>
  <text x="712" y="512" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#E2E8F0">not just within individual sessions.</text>
  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="1240" y="700" text-anchor="end" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">2 / 8</text>
</svg>

      <stop offset="0%" stop-color="#3B82F6" stop-opacity="0.05"/>
      <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#3B82F6" stop-opacity="0"/>

  </defs>
  <!-- Background -->
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="#0F1729"/>
  <rect width="1280" height="720" fill="url(#bgGlow)"/>
  <!-- Title -->
  <rect x="40" y="40" width="6" height="36" fill="url(#titleGrad)" rx="3"/>
  <text x="60" y="68" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="26" font-weight="bold" fill="#E2E8F0">Three Properties That Distinguish SkillClaw</text>

  <!-- Property 1: Collective Evolution -->
  <rect x="60" y="110" width="1160" height="150" rx="12" fill="#1A2744" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="110" width="6" height="150" fill="#3B82F6" rx="3"/>
  <circle cx="110" cy="155" r="24" fill="#3B82F6" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
  <text x="110" y="161" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#3B82F6">1</text>
  <text x="150" y="150" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#E2E8F0">Collective Evolution</text>
  <use data-icon="users" x="370" y="133" width="24" height="24" fill="#3B82F6"/>
  <text x="150" y="182" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">Knowledge from individual interactions contributes to a shared, continuously improving skill ecosystem.</text>
  <text x="150" y="210" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">Cross-user trajectory aggregation provides complementary behavioral signals that a single user cannot generate alone.</text>
  <rect x="150" y="228" width="1040" height="1" fill="#334155" fill-opacity="0.3"/>
  <text x="150" y="248" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#3B82F6">Individual sessions → System-level knowledge accumulation</text>

  <!-- Property 2: Fully Automatic -->
  <rect x="60" y="280" width="1160" height="150" rx="12" fill="#1A2744" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="280" width="6" height="150" fill="#06B6D4" rx="3"/>
  <circle cx="110" cy="325" r="24" fill="#06B6D4" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
  <text x="110" y="331" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#06B6D4">2</text>
  <text x="150" y="320" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#E2E8F0">Fully Automatic</text>
  <use data-icon="cog" x="320" y="303" width="24" height="24" fill="#06B6D4"/>
  <text x="150" y="352" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">Skill evolution is driven by runtime interaction without manual curation or explicit user intervention.</text>
  <text x="150" y="380" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">No human-in-the-loop required — the system autonomously identifies improvement opportunities from usage patterns.</text>
  <rect x="150" y="398" width="1040" height="1" fill="#334155" fill-opacity="0.3"/>
  <text x="150" y="418" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#06B6D4">Zero manual curation → Continuous autonomous improvement</text>

  <!-- Property 3: Agentic Evolution Paradigm -->
  <rect x="60" y="450" width="1160" height="150" rx="12" fill="#1A2744" filter="url(#cardShadow)"/>
  <rect x="60" y="450" width="6" height="150" fill="#8B5CF6" rx="3"/>
  <circle cx="110" cy="495" r="24" fill="#8B5CF6" fill-opacity="0.15"/>
  <text x="110" y="501" text-anchor="middle" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="16" font-weight="bold" fill="#8B5CF6">3</text>
  <text x="150" y="490" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="22" font-weight="bold" fill="#E2E8F0">Agentic Evolution Paradigm</text>
  <use data-icon="sparkles" x="430" y="473" width="24" height="24" fill="#8B5CF6"/>
  <text x="150" y="522" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="17" fill="#94A3B8">Skill updates are produced through open-ended reasoning rather than predefined update rules.</text>
  <text x="150" y="550" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#64748B">The agentic evolver's Evidence → Attribution → Evolution pipeline enables context-aware skill mutations.</text>
  <rect x="150" y="568" width="1040" height="1" fill="#334155" fill-opacity="0.3"/>
  <text x="150" y="588" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14" fill="#8B5CF6">Predefined rules → Open-ended agent reasoning over evidence</text>

  <!-- Implication box -->
  <rect x="60" y="630" width="1160" height="56" rx="10" fill="#3B82F6" fill-opacity="0.08"/>
  <use data-icon="lightbulb" x="80" y="643" width="28" height="28" fill="#3B82F6"/>
  <text x="118" y="658" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif" font-size="15" font-weight="bold" fill="#3B82F6">Implication:</text>
  <text x="222" y="658" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#E2E8F0">SkillClaw points toward a future where agent systems continuously improve through collective usage — </text>
  <text x="118" y="678" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="15" fill="#E2E8F0">every interaction becomes a potential source of system-wide enhancement.</text>

  <!-- Footer -->
  <text x="1240" y="700" text-anchor="end" font-family="Calibri, Arial, sans-serif" font-size="11" fill="#64748B">8 / 8</text>
</svg>

arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome to this presentation on SkillClaw, a framework for collective skill evolution in multi-user LLM agent ecosystems. Today we'll explore how agent skills can continuously improve by aggregating cross-user interaction trajectories and applying agentic, evidence-driven updates. This work addresses a fundamental limitation in current agent systems — the inability to learn and evolve from runtime experience.

Key points: (1) SkillClaw introduces collective skill evolution (2) Framework for multi-user LLM agent ecosystems (3) Published on arXiv
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_problem_static_skills

[Transition] Before diving into the solution, let's understand the problem we're solving.

Current LLM agents like OpenClaw rely on reusable skills, but these skills remain static after deployment. Users manually install skills from a centralized hub, and solutions discovered during interaction never persist beyond individual sessions. [Pause] The same failures are rediscovered independently by different users, over and over again. Existing approaches — whether memory-based or skill-based — fail to bridge this gap. Memory methods stay tied to specific instances, while skill methods treat the library as a static resource that never evolves.

Key points: (1) Skills are static after deployment (2) Knowledge doesn't accumulate across users (3) Existing approaches are insufficient
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_architecture_overview

[Transition] So how does SkillClaw solve this? With a closed-loop pipeline connecting multi-user interaction to shared skill evolution.

The architecture follows four stages. First, independent agents interact with their environments and produce structured session trajectories. These are aggregated across users and grouped by referenced skills. Then the agentic evolver analyzes each group through three stages: Evidence, Attribution, and Evolution. [Pause] Finally, updated skills are verified and synchronized back to all agents — completing the loop. What makes this powerful is that the evolution is driven by an autonomous agent performing open-ended reasoning, not predefined update rules.

Key points: (1) Four-stage closed loop (2) Cross-user trajectory aggregation (3) Autonomous agent-driven evolution
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_agentic_evolver_pipeline

[Transition] Let's zoom into the agentic evolver — the engine that drives skill improvement.

The evolver works in three stages. Stage one, Evidence: it analyzes trajectories to identify behavioral patterns across users. Stage two, Attribution: it diagnoses the root causes of both failures and successes, separating generalizable improvements from idiosyncratic fixes. Stage three, Evolution: it proposes skill mutations — either refining existing skills or creating entirely new ones. [Pause] The critical distinction here is that this is open-ended agent reasoning, not template-based or rule-based updates. The evolver adapts to the specific patterns it observes in the evidence.

Key points: (1) Three-stage pipeline: Evidence, Attribution, Evolution (2) Open-ended reasoning, not predefined rules (3) Context-aware skill mutations
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_cross_user_aggregation

[Transition] A natural question is: why do we need multiple users? Can't a single user generate enough signal?

The answer is no. Different users exercise the same skill under diverse contexts, producing complementary views of that skill's behavioral boundary. One user might reveal where a skill succeeds, while another exposes where it breaks — under conditions the first user never encountered. [Pause] A single user rarely generates enough signal to separate a generalizable improvement from an idiosyncratic fix. SkillClaw is compatible with a range of Claw-style systems including OpenClaw, CoPaw, IronClaw, and several others, enabling broad trajectory collection. Evaluation on WildClawBench with Qwen3-Max demonstrates substantial improvements.

Key points: (1) Multi-user signals are complementary (2) Single user insufficient for generalizable improvements (3) Compatible across seven Claw-style systems
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_case_study_creative

[Transition] Let's look at how this plays out in practice with two case studies, starting with the multimodal creative pipeline.

Over six days, the system evaluated six candidate skills. Only one — the initial workspace validator on Day 1 — was accepted. Every subsequent attempt to evolve the creative pipeline was rejected by the validator. [Pause] This illustrates the conservative verification process at work. With an acceptance rate of just 16.7%, the system clearly favors stability over novelty when evidence doesn't support improvement. This prevents regressions and protects skill quality.

Key points: (1) 1 of 6 candidates accepted (2) Conservative verification prevents regressions (3) System protects existing quality
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 07_case_study_git

[Transition] Now contrast that with the git push auth-fallback skill, which tells a very different story.

Here, 3 of 6 days yielded accepted updates. The skill was successfully refined three times in succession — adding safe fallbacks, unifying filenames, and fixing subshell pitfalls. Day 4 confirmed the current pool was already optimal. Then Days 5 and 6 were rejected — the skill had reached a natural plateau. [Pause] This 50% acceptance rate, compared to 16.7% for the creative pipeline, shows that when evidence genuinely supports improvement, the system accepts updates. It's not uniformly conservative — it's evidence-driven.

Key points: (1) 3 of 6 accepted — iterative refinement works (2) Natural plateau detection (3) Evidence-driven, not uniformly conservative
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] Let me leave you with three properties that distinguish SkillClaw from existing approaches.

First, collective evolution: individual interactions improve a shared ecosystem, not just a single user's experience. Second, fully automatic: no manual curation or user intervention required — the system improves autonomously. Third, the agentic evolution paradigm: open-ended reasoning replaces predefined rules. [Pause] The implication is profound. SkillClaw points toward a future where every interaction with an agent system becomes a potential source of system-wide enhancement. Agent skills don't just execute — they evolve.

Key points: (1) Collective, automatic, agentic (2) Every interaction improves the system (3) Path toward continuously improving agents
Duration: 2 minutes
